bibl.title: Hippocampal-prefrontal input supports spatial encoding in working memory

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the direct ventral hippocampus to medial prefrontal cortex projection during spatial working memory
span.quote: While the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus are known to jointly contribute to successful spatial working memory, the anatomical pathway and temporal window for interaction of these structures critical to spatial working memory has not yet been established.

span.label: which phase of spatial working memory requires this pathway, what it carries, and by what anatomical route
span.quote: It remains unclear, however, which phase(s) of SWM (encoding, maintenance, and/or retrieval) require the joint participation of the HPC and mPFC, what behaviorally relevant information is conveyed between the two structures, and by what anatomical pathway(s) they interact.

span.label: shows the pathway is needed for encoding but not maintenance or retrieval, both behaviourally and in the prefrontal representation, with gamma synchrony as the carrier
span.quote: Here, we find that direct hippocampal-prefrontal afferents are critical for encoding, but not for maintenance or retrieval, of spatial cues.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Here, we find that direct hippocampal-prefrontal afferents are critical for encoding, but not for maintenance or retrieval, of spatial cues.

span.label: spatial working memory
span.quote: Spatial working memory (SWM) is an essential feature of goal-directed action.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Therefore, recordings of multiple single units were obtained from the prelimbic region of the mPFC in mice performing the 4-goal task ( Extended Data Fig. 1 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Gamma-frequency synchronization between vHPC and mPFC carries the spatial cue across the direct projection, so that entrainment of mPFC spikes to vHPC gamma is what enables successful encoding.
span.quote: Successful encoding of these cues appears to be mediated by gamma-frequency synchrony between the two structures.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: vHPC gamma oscillations entrain vHPC output in phase, which then influences mPFC spike timing at monosynaptic delays, making spike entrainment the physical signature of the signal being propagated.
span.quote: These findings demonstrate that entrainment of mPFC spikes to vHPC gamma oscillations is a physiological signature of task-critical long-range signal propagation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The vHPC input acts excitatorily on mPFC units, driving the location-selective elevation of firing rate that constitutes the cue representation.
span.quote: These results reveal an excitatory role for vHPC input in the location-selective firing rate enhancement seen in mPFC units.

span.label: vHPC input drives a selective firing-rate elevation in each unit's preferred goal, without changing baseline rates
span.quote: The effect of Sample Light was striking. Inhibition of terminals during the sample phase prevented the increase in firing rate that occurred in units’ preferred goals, without affecting baseline rates ( Fig. 4c , top). The same results were obtained when including all units in the analysis ( Extended Data Fig. 5 ). These results reveal an excitatory role for vHPC input in the location-selective firing rate enhancement seen in mPFC units.

span.label: the same goal selectivity persists during choice runs and no longer needs vHPC input, so physiology mirrors the behavioural dissociation
span.quote: However, unlike in sample runs, this elevation was unaffected by vHPC-mPFC terminal inhibition ( Fig. 4d ). In this finding, physiology mirrored the behavioral result, indicating that goal selectivity following encoding is no longer dependent on vHPC input.

span.label: vHPC gamma leads mPFC spiking at lags consistent with monosynaptic transmission, and terminal inhibition reduces that phase-locking
span.quote: Consistent with this suggestion, inhibition of vHPC-mPFC terminals reduced the overall strength of gamma phase-locking ( Fig. 5g-h ), indicating that the observed synchrony is mediated by direct vHPC-mPFC input.

span.label: the directionality is specific to gamma: in theta the mPFC leads, and theta synchrony survives terminal inhibition
span.quote: Importantly, this directionality was specific to gamma oscillations, as lag analysis of phase-locking in the theta range revealed an opposite directionality; mPFC led vHPC (but not dHPC) activity in the theta range, and theta synchrony was unaffected by terminal inhibition

span.label: terminal illumination suppresses transmission without silencing the source cells, which is what makes the manipulation projection-specific
span.quote: In the awake, resting state, light pulses delivered to vHPC reduced local spontaneous multiunit activity by ~50% ( Fig. 1d ), while illumination of terminal fields in the mPFC had no effect on multi-unit activity in the vHPC

span.label: a four-goal maze prevents the animal from forming a spatially directed plan until the choice phase, which is what separates encoding from retrieval
span.quote: To better segregate the encoding, maintenance, and retrieval phases within each trial, a modified, 4-goal T-maze was constructed ( Fig. 2c ). Here, as in the 2-goal task, a single goal was made available for retrieval of the sample reward. During the choice run, the sample goal and one of the other three arms were open. This design prevents the mouse from formulating a spatially-directed action plan until the choice phase, when, at the end of its center arm run, it is presented with two of the four goals as options ( Supplementary Video ). Thus, selection of the choice goal was temporally restricted to the choice phase, separating out encoding from retrieval.

span.label: The authors cannot definitively exclude an effect of terminal inhibition during the choice (retrieval) phase; the null result there was underpowered.
span.quote: Although we cannot conclusively rule out an effect of terminal inhibition during choice, these experiments indicate that input from the vHPC to the mPFC is critical for encoding of spatial cues.

span.label: Retrospective location coding might exist in mPFC in a form their decoding analysis could not detect (e.g. synaptic weights or very brief reactivation).
span.quote: We cannot, however, rule out the possibility that retrospective location is persistently represented in the mPFC in a form not detectable using the analytic techniques presented here, such as in temporary changes in synaptic weights, or transient reactivation that is too brief to be reliably decoded from binned spike histograms.

span.label: The pseudo-population decoding approach assumes comparable spike statistics across animals and sessions and discards correlated variability.
span.quote: This approach assumes equivalent spike statistics across animals and recording sessions, and ignores potential contributions to population coding from correlated spike variability that would be observed if all units were indeed simultaneously recorded

span.label: The gamma phase-locking effect is small: under 10% of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked even at the best lag.
span.quote: This phenomenon is subtle – at the lag with the greatest phase-locking, fewer than 10% of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked to vHPC gamma.

span.label: the choice-phase null is not conclusive; an n of 37 per group would have been needed to detect the observed effect size
span.quote: In the Choice Light condition (repeated here with either 10 or 20 second delays), a slight trend toward impairment did not reach significance, and post-hoc power analysis revealed that an n of 37 animals/group would have been required to detect a paired difference given the observed effect size.

span.label: the authors state plainly that they cannot conclusively rule out an effect during choice
span.quote: Although we cannot conclusively rule out an effect of terminal inhibition during choice, these experiments indicate that input from the vHPC to the mPFC is critical for encoding of spatial cues.

span.label: the absence of retrospective coding is scoped to the analysis: it could be held in synaptic weights or in reactivation too brief to decode from binned histograms
span.quote: We cannot, however, rule out the possibility that retrospective location is persistently represented in the mPFC in a form not detectable using the analytic techniques presented here, such as in temporary changes in synaptic weights, or transient reactivation that is too brief to be reliably decoded from binned spike histograms.

span.label: the gamma effect is subtle - fewer than 10% of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked at the best lag
span.quote: This phenomenon is subtle – at the lag with the greatest phase-locking, fewer than 10% of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked to vHPC gamma.

span.label: the promoter was changed between the two behavioural experiments, so they are not methodologically identical
span.quote: The hSynapsin promoter was chosen for the 4-goal experiment to account for possible long-range GABAergic vHPC-mPFC projections and to avoid potential toxicity effects resulting from opsin expression under the stronger CamKII

span.label: male mice only
span.quote: Male C57BL/6 mice (Jackson Labs) were used for all experiments, aged 8-12 weeks at first use.

span.label: the theta result ran counter to the authors' initial hypotheses and is reported as such
span.quote: The finding that mPFC theta activity leads vHPC theta, and that theta synchrony between the two structures did not appear to depend upon vHPC-mPFC afferents, ran counter to our initial hypotheses.

span.label: delay-period persistent firing as the expected mechanism, imported and then not found in the rodent homologue
span.quote: The primate dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is functionally analogous to, but anatomically distinct from, the rodent prelimbic region of the mPFC

span.label: a maximum margin linear classifier with cross-validation, used to read location from distributed population rates
span.quote: Given the inhomogeneous and distributed nature of the representation of spatial information among recorded mPFC units, a maximum margin linear classifier 22 was used to decode sample goal location from binned population firing rate vectors and to quantify the strength and reliability of the neural representation

span.label: a CamKIIα-mCherry virus carrying no opsin, run in the acute stimulation/silencing and 2-goal t-maze experiments
span.quote: In the acute stimulation/silencing experiment and the 2-goal t-maze experiment, a CamKIIα-eArch3.0-eYFP sequence was used to express the opsin and CamKIIα-mCherry was used as an opsin-negative control.

span.label: the researcher who trained and ran the mice was blinded to viral group by a second lab member, who did the assignment
span.quote: The researcher responsible for training and running the mice was blinded as to viral group by another lab member, who randomly assigned opsin and control viruses.

span.label: encoding, maintenance and retrieval are defined by TRIAL PHASE and made separable by a maze redesign - the distinction is built into the apparatus, not read off the behaviour
span.quote: To better segregate the encoding, maintenance, and retrieval phases within each trial, a modified, 4-goal T-maze was constructed ( Fig. 2c ). Here, as in the 2-goal task, a single goal was made available for retrieval of the sample reward. During the choice run, the sample goal and one of the other three arms were open. This design prevents the mouse from formulating a spatially-directed action plan until the choice phase, when, at the end of its center arm run, it is presented with two of the four goals as options ( Supplementary Video ). Thus, selection of the choice goal was temporally restricted to the choice phase, separating out encoding from retrieval.

span.label: projection-specific means the terminals are silenced where they arrive, not the cells that send them - validated by showing vHPC firing is untouched by mPFC illumination
span.quote: In the awake, resting state, light pulses delivered to vHPC reduced local spontaneous multiunit activity by ~50% ( Fig. 1d ), while illumination of terminal fields in the mPFC had no effect on multi-unit activity in the vHPC

span.label: no evidence of retrospective coding is scoped explicitly to the analytic technique, naming two forms it could take and still be missed
span.quote: We cannot, however, rule out the possibility that retrospective location is persistently represented in the mPFC in a form not detectable using the analytic techniques presented here, such as in temporary changes in synaptic weights, or transient reactivation that is too brief to be reliably decoded from binned spike histograms.

span.label: functionally analogous but anatomically distinct - the stated relation between primate dorsolateral PFC and rodent prelimbic cortex, which licenses comparing them cautiously
span.quote: The primate dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is functionally analogous to, but anatomically distinct from, the rodent prelimbic region of the mPFC

span.label: builds-on → Wang et al., 2006 (adaptive intra-trial delay procedure for the T-maze task)
span.quote: Also in the 2-goal experiment only, to minimize across-session performance drift, and ceiling effects, intra-trial delay was adjusted according to the preceding day's performance, beginning at 10sec and progressively increasing delay by an additional 5 seconds following days on which performance was above 80% (as in Wang et al., 2006).

span.label: qualifies → prior reports of retrospective and prospective location coding in rodent mPFC during delays
span.quote: But retrospective place firing has been shown to be absent in rodent mPFC when past and future location are independent

span.label: reinterprets → the earlier finding that vHPC silencing reduces dHPC-mPFC theta synchrony, proposing it was an indirect effect on dHPC
span.quote: The current findings regarding theta synchrony suggest there may be an alternative explanation for the previous finding of reduced dHPC-mPFC synchrony with vHPC silencing. It is possible that pharmacological inactivation of vHPC affected downstream targets in the dHPC, disrupting dHPC theta activity and thus dHPC-mPFC theta synchrony. This possibility is supported by the finding that vHPC silencing with muscimol reduces dHPC theta power

span.label: extends → work implicating vHPC and mPFC in contextual learning, by moving it to a seconds timescale
span.quote: The combined results that vHPC-mPFC input is necessary only during cue encoding, that mPFC lacks retrospective location representation during maintenance and retrieval, and that mPFC representation of contemporaneous location during retrieval is not dependent on direct vHPC input, suggest that the mPFC processes sample goal location transiently and that some downstream structure(s) may maintain the information thereafter. Likely candidate structures would include dHPC and the thalamic nucleus reuniens.

span.label: contradicts → persistent prefrontal firing as the mechanism maintaining the cue between encoding and retrieval
span.quote: Interestingly, we find no evidence of retrospective location coding in mPFC activity ( Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3 ). Within the parameters of this study, this argues against persistent firing within mPFC neurons as a means of maintaining the stimulus representation between encoding and retrieval.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · vHPC —causes→ mPFC
span.quote: Here, we find that direct hippocampal-prefrontal afferents are critical for encoding, but not for maintenance or retrieval, of spatial cues.

span.label: encoding —contrasted-with→ retrieval
span.quote: Here, we find that direct hippocampal-prefrontal afferents are critical for encoding, but not for maintenance or retrieval, of spatial cues.

span.label: gamma —contrasted-with→ theta
span.quote: Importantly, this directionality was specific to gamma oscillations, as lag analysis of phase-locking in the theta range revealed an opposite directionality; mPFC led vHPC (but not dHPC) activity in the theta range, and theta synchrony was unaffected by terminal inhibition

span.label: spatial working memory —operationalised-as→ delayed non-match-to-place
span.quote: To better segregate the encoding, maintenance, and retrieval phases within each trial, a modified, 4-goal T-maze was constructed ( Fig. 2c ). Here, as in the 2-goal task, a single goal was made available for retrieval of the sample reward. During the choice run, the sample goal and one of the other three arms were open. This design prevents the mouse from formulating a spatially-directed action plan until the choice phase, when, at the end of its center arm run, it is presented with two of the four goals as options ( Supplementary Video ). Thus, selection of the choice goal was temporally restricted to the choice phase, separating out encoding from retrieval.

span.label: gamma —operationalised-as→ pairwise phase consistency
span.quote: Therefore, long-range synchrony was quantified using the magnitude (pairwise phase consistency, PPC 26 ) and significance (Rayleigh's test 9 ) of phase non-uniformity of spike times in one brain region relative to LFP oscillations in another.

span.label: vHPC —causes→ mPFC
span.quote: Direct HPC-mPFC connectivity is confined to a unidirectional projection from the CA1/subiculum of the ventral-most two-thirds of the hippocampus (vHPC)

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: 44% of mPFC single units displayed selectivity for one or both spatial dimensions that distinguished goal arms (left/right, back/front), and/or their interaction, as assayed by 2-way ANOVA ( Extended Data Fig. 2a-d ).

span.label: repeated-measures ANOVA
span.quote: All ANOVA tests involving multiple observations per subject/unit (every figure except Extended Fig. 2D ) were done as repeated measures group-by-condition tests.

span.label: paired t-test
span.quote: All independence testing of paired values (i.e. changes across conditions) utilized paired t-tests or (where stated) signed rank tests.

span.label: Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons
span.quote: All t-tests and rank tests performed with more than 2 groups were done post-hoc to ANOVA tests except where Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons is specifically cited.

span.label: significance threshold (alpha)
span.quote: All effects presented as statistically significant exceeded an α-threshold of 0.05.

span.label: Rayleigh test of circular uniformity
span.quote: Therefore, long-range synchrony was quantified using the magnitude (pairwise phase consistency, PPC 26 ) and significance (Rayleigh's test 9 ) of phase non-uniformity of spike times in one brain region relative to LFP oscillations in another.

span.label: pairwise phase consistency (spike-field phase-locking measure)
span.quote: Phase-locking of spikes to the oscillatory phase of LFPs was performed using pairwise phase consistency, which, unlike other commonly used measures of phase-locking, is unbiased by spike number 26 .

span.label: linear classifier / population decoding
span.quote: A maximum margin linear classifier was used to decode sample goal location from binned population firing rate vectors and to quantify the strength and reliability of the neural representation.

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: The classifier was cross-validated by training on data from half of the trials and testing the model's performance on data from the remainder (see Methods).

span.label: resampling with replacement (bootstrap)
span.quote: At each test phase 100 test vectors per condition are randomly resampled with replacement, and the performance of the model is quantified as the average accuracy in classifying them.

span.label: statistical power analysis / effect size
span.quote: In the Choice Light condition (repeated here with either 10 or 20 second delays), a slight trend toward impairment did not reach significance, and post-hoc power analysis revealed that an n of 37 animals/group would have been required to detect a paired difference given the observed effect size.

span.label: maximum margin linear classifier, cross-validated
span.quote: Given the inhomogeneous and distributed nature of the representation of spatial information among recorded mPFC units, a maximum margin linear classifier 22 was used to decode sample goal location from binned population firing rate vectors and to quantify the strength and reliability of the neural representation

span.label: pairwise phase consistency
span.quote: Therefore, long-range synchrony was quantified using the magnitude (pairwise phase consistency, PPC 26 ) and significance (Rayleigh's test 9 ) of phase non-uniformity of spike times in one brain region relative to LFP oscillations in another.

span.label: Rayleigh's test
span.quote: Therefore, long-range synchrony was quantified using the magnitude (pairwise phase consistency, PPC 26 ) and significance (Rayleigh's test 9 ) of phase non-uniformity of spike times in one brain region relative to LFP oscillations in another.

span.label: post-hoc power analysis
span.quote: In the Choice Light condition (repeated here with either 10 or 20 second delays), a slight trend toward impairment did not reach significance, and post-hoc power analysis revealed that an n of 37 animals/group would have been required to detect a paired difference given the observed effect size.

span.label: Optogenetically silencing vHPC-to-mPFC terminals during the sample run impairs delayed non-match-to-place performance in opsin-expressing mice, while the same silencing during the entire trial also impairs it and silencing during choice does not reach significance.
span.quote: In Arch + but not Arch − mice, performance was impaired in Entire Trial and Sample Light conditions; Choice Light did not result in a statistically significant impairment ( Fig. 2b ).

span.label: In a redesigned 4-goal maze that separates encoding from retrieval, sample-phase silencing again impaired performance, confirming the pathway is required specifically for encoding.
span.quote: Again, performance was impaired in the Sample Light condition, confirming the requirement for vHPC-mPFC input during encoding ( Fig. 2d ).

span.label: Silencing the pathway during the memory delay produced no significant behavioural impairment.
span.quote: There was also no significant impairment with terminal illumination during the delay period ( Delay Light ; Fig. 2d ).

span.label: Population decoding of the sample goal from mPFC units was abolished (reduced to chance) by terminal illumination in Arch-expressing mice but was unchanged in Arch-negative controls.
span.quote: For Arch − animals, sample goal was decoded equally well with or without mPFC illumination, while in Arch + animals accuracy was reduced to chance by mPFC illumination ( Fig. 3c ).

span.label: Sample-phase terminal inhibition removed the firing-rate increase that goal-selective mPFC units show at their preferred goal, while leaving their baseline rates intact.
span.quote: Inhibition of terminals during the sample phase prevented the increase in firing rate that occurred in units’ preferred goals, without affecting baseline rates ( Fig. 4c , top).

span.label: During choice runs the same goal-selective firing-rate elevation persisted despite terminal inhibition, so mPFC location coding at retrieval does not need the direct vHPC input.
span.quote: However, unlike in sample runs, this elevation was unaffected by vHPC-mPFC terminal inhibition ( Fig. 4d ).

span.label: Terminal inhibition did not change overall mPFC firing rates, either pooled or split into putative pyramidal cells and interneurons.
span.quote: Overall firing rates of mPFC units were unaffected by terminal illumination in both Arch − and Arch + animals, whether all were considered together ( Fig. 4a ), or if putative pyramidal cells and interneurons were separated based on waveform features ( Extended Data Fig. 4 ).

span.label: Decoding of the non-spatial task phase from mPFC firing survived sample-phase terminal inhibition, showing the deficit is specific to spatial cues rather than a general encoding failure.
span.quote: When the decoder was trained on firing rates from this epoch in No Light trials and tested on choice runs from Sample Light trials, model accuracy was not affected ( Fig. 3e ), suggesting that vHPC-mPFC terminal inhibition does not generally interfere with the encoding of task-relevant information.

span.label: A subset of mPFC units phase-locked to vHPC gamma, and phase-locking was strongest at lags where vHPC gamma preceded mPFC spiking, indicating vHPC leads mPFC in the gamma band.
span.quote: A subset of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked to vHPC gamma ( Fig. 5b-c ), and the percentage of significantly phase-locked units was greatest at lags in which vHPC gamma preceded mPFC spiking ( Fig. 5c ).

span.label: Inhibiting the vHPC-mPFC terminals weakened gamma phase-locking, showing the long-range gamma synchrony depends on the direct anatomical projection.
span.quote: Consistent with this suggestion, inhibition of vHPC-mPFC terminals reduced the overall strength of gamma phase-locking ( Fig. 5g-h ), indicating that the observed synchrony is mediated by direct vHPC-mPFC input.

span.label: In the theta band the directionality reversed - mPFC led vHPC - and theta synchrony was not affected by silencing the pathway.
span.quote: mPFC led vHPC (but not dHPC) activity in the theta range, and theta synchrony was unaffected by terminal inhibition ( Extended Data Fig. 7 ).

span.label: Gamma phase-locking was stronger during sample runs than choice runs, and stronger on correct than incorrect sample runs, tying the synchrony to successful encoding.
span.quote: PPC values were higher during sample than choice runs, demonstrating that stronger gamma phase-locking is associated with the encoding phase of the trial ( Fig. 5i ).

span.label: Additionally, gamma phase-locking during sample runs distinguished correct from incorrect trials.
span.quote: Additionally, phase-locking was stronger during sample runs of correct trials than of incorrect trials ( Fig. 5j ), suggesting that it may support effective encoding of location cues.

span.label: The mPFC showed no retrospective coding of the previously visited location, arguing against persistent mPFC firing as the storage mechanism during the delay.
span.quote: Interestingly, we find no evidence of retrospective location coding in mPFC activity ( Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3 ).

span.label: inhibiting the direct pathway during the sample phase impairs performance; during delay or choice it does not
span.quote: There was also no significant impairment with terminal illumination during the delay period ( Delay Light ; Fig. 2d ).

span.label: sample goal is decoded from prefrontal population activity at 96% on arrival at the goal
span.quote: Sample goal identity was decoded from the mPFC population at accuracies well above chance from the time the animals entered the T-intersection, and peaked at 96% upon arrival at the reward port in the sample goal

span.label: inhibiting the pathway during encoding drops that decoding to chance in opsin-expressing animals only
span.quote: For Arch − animals, sample goal was decoded equally well with or without mPFC illumination, while in Arch + animals accuracy was reduced to chance by mPFC illumination ( Fig. 3c ). This result demonstrates that vHPC input is critical for the representation of sample goal among mPFC units during encoding.

span.label: the same manipulation leaves task-phase decoding at 0.98, so it does not impair encoding generally
span.quote: When the decoder was trained on firing rates from this epoch in No Light trials and tested on choice runs from Sample Light trials, model accuracy was not affected ( Fig. 3e ), suggesting that vHPC-mPFC terminal inhibition does not generally interfere with the encoding of task-relevant information.

span.label: overall firing rates are unchanged; only the goal-selective elevation is lost
span.quote: Overall firing rates of mPFC units were unaffected by terminal illumination in both Arch − and Arch + animals, whether all were considered together ( Fig. 4a ), or if putative pyramidal cells and interneurons were separated based on waveform features

span.label: goal selectivity during choice runs survives the same inhibition, mirroring the behaviour
span.quote: However, unlike in sample runs, this elevation was unaffected by vHPC-mPFC terminal inhibition ( Fig. 4d ). In this finding, physiology mirrored the behavioral result, indicating that goal selectivity following encoding is no longer dependent on vHPC input.

span.label: vHPC gamma leads mPFC spiking, and terminal inhibition weakens that phase-locking
span.quote: A subset of mPFC units were significantly phase-locked to vHPC gamma ( Fig. 5b-c ), and the percentage of significantly phase-locked units was greatest at lags in which vHPC gamma preceded mPFC spiking

span.label: in theta the direction reverses and synchrony is unaffected by the same manipulation
span.quote: Importantly, this directionality was specific to gamma oscillations, as lag analysis of phase-locking in the theta range revealed an opposite directionality; mPFC led vHPC (but not dHPC) activity in the theta range, and theta synchrony was unaffected by terminal inhibition

span.label: gamma phase-locking is stronger on sample than choice runs, and stronger on correct than incorrect trials
span.quote: PPC values were higher during sample than choice runs, demonstrating that stronger gamma phase-locking is associated with the encoding phase of the trial ( Fig. 5i ). Additionally, phase-locking was stronger during sample runs of correct trials than of incorrect trials ( Fig. 5j ), suggesting that it may support effective encoding of location cues.

span.label: no retrospective location coding was found in mPFC during the delay
span.quote: Interestingly, we find no evidence of retrospective location coding in mPFC activity ( Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3 ). Within the parameters of this study, this argues against persistent firing within mPFC neurons as a means of maintaining the stimulus representation between encoding and retrieval.

span.label: spatial working memory
span.quote: Spatial working memory, the caching of behaviorally relevant spatial cues on a timescale of seconds, is a fundamental constituent of cognition.

span.label: vHPC (the direct hippocampal-prefrontal projection)
span.quote: Direct HPC-mPFC connectivity is confined to a unidirectional projection from the CA1/subiculum of the ventral-most two-thirds of the hippocampus (vHPC) 13 - 15 .

span.label: sample (encoding) phase of the DNMTP task
span.term: sample (encoding) phase of the DNMTP task
span.quote: In the sample phase, one of two goal locations is blocked by a wall, and the mouse is directed toward a food reward in the open location; during this phase the animal must encode the location of the sample goal.

span.label: delay (maintenance) phase of the DNMTP task
span.term: delay (maintenance) phase of the DNMTP task
span.quote: In the delay phase, the mouse returns to the start box and must maintain the sample goal in working memory during a variable delay (Methods).

span.label: a unit's preferred goal
span.quote: Each unit's preferred goal (that in which firing rate was most different from the mean rate across the other three goals) was identified using weights generated by the classifier (Methods).

span.label: spatial working memory
span.quote: While the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus are known to jointly contribute to successful spatial working memory, the anatomical pathway and temporal window for interaction of these structures critical to spatial working memory has not yet been established.

span.label: lag analysis for directionality
span.quote: To determine the temporal directionality of synchronous activity, lag analysis was performed, in which phase-locking was calculated at various temporal shifts; preferential phase-locking at a nonzero lag indicates a predictive relationship between oscillatory phase and spike timing.

span.label: trial phase in which vHPC-mPFC terminals were optogenetically illuminated (entire trial / sample / delay / choice)
span.term: trial phase in which vHPC-mPFC terminals were optogenetically illuminated (entire trial / sample / delay / choice)
span.quote: Following successful task acquisition, light was delivered to vHPC-mPFC terminal fields in Arch + and Arch − mice during the Entire Trial , the sample phase only ( Sample Light ), or the choice phase only ( Choice Light ).

span.label: opsin-negative control virus (mCherry / eYFP without Arch)
span.term: opsin-negative control virus (mCherry / eYFP without Arch)
span.quote: In the acute stimulation/silencing experiment and the 2-goal t-maze experiment, a CamKIIα-eArch3.0-eYFP sequence was used to express the opsin and CamKIIα-mCherry was used as an opsin-negative control.

span.label: intra-trial delay duration, held at 10 s
span.term: intra-trial delay duration, held at 10 s
span.quote: To allow for direct comparison of delay within animals in this task, intra-trial delay was fixed at 10sec, with the addition of a single session of 20sec delays as the final session for each animal.

span.label: DNMTP task performance (fraction correct)
span.quote: In Arch + but not Arch − mice, performance was impaired in Entire Trial and Sample Light conditions; Choice Light did not result in a statistically significant impairment ( Fig. 2b ).

span.quote: Sample goal identity was decoded from the mPFC population at accuracies well above chance from the time the animals entered the T-intersection, and peaked at 96% upon arrival at the reward port in the sample goal ( Fig. 3b ).

span.quote: There was also no significant impairment with terminal illumination during the delay period ( Delay Light ; Fig. 2d ).

span.quote: To determine the temporal directionality of synchronous activity, lag analysis was performed, in which phase-locking was calculated at various temporal shifts; preferential phase-locking at a nonzero lag indicates a predictive relationship between oscillatory phase and spike timing.
